To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
UHPFRC containing steel fibers and CNTs has a high electrical conductivity and a self-sensing capacity that can be activated by the formation and growth of cracks.

the electrical conductivity of ultra-high-performance concrete with carbon nanotubes can be improved by adding steel fibers and that the self-sensing capacity under compression and flexural loading can be improved by including a certain amount of carbon nanotubes.

the self-sensing capacity under compression of UHPF RC with carbon nanotubes was activated by the development of cracks and the pre-cracking self sensing capacity of UHPFR C with carbon nanotub es was more effective under tension than under compression.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the electrical and selfsensing capacities of UHPRFRC with and without CNTs.
the development of a new type of UHPF RC with self-sensing properties that is suitable for use in smart structural applications.
the electrical properties and self-sensing capacity under both tensile and compressive stress states of UHPF RC with and without CNTs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the electrical conductivity and the self-sensing capacity can be enhanced by incorporating steel fibers and CNTs into UHPFRC.
UHPFRC containing steel fibers and CNTs has great potential for use in structural health monitoring.
UHPFRC has the potential for electrical conductivity and piezoresisitivity, but the self-sensing capacity can be significantly improved by adding CNTs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the electrical and self sensing capacities of UHPFRCS with CNTs are strongly influenced by the CNT content, and the pre-cracking self sensing capacity of UHPFRCC is better under tension state than under compression state.
the electrical conductivity of CNT-incorporated UHPFRC is significantly improved, and the pre-cracking self- sensing capacity is activated when the CNT content is 0.3%, or greater, by volume.
CNTs can effectively improve the self-sensing capacity, especially the pre-cracking self sensing capacity, of UHPFRR under flexure.
The main takeaway from our work is that

UHPFRC can be used as a smart concrete with self-sensing capacities that are activated by crack formation, and that the piezoresistivity of UHPF is more pronounced under flexure than under compression.

UHPFRC can be used to sense the formation of cracks and the pre-peak behavior under flexure, and that the sensing capacity of UHPRC with CNT can be improved with a proper selection of steel fiber content and fiber orientation.

UHPFRC can be used as an electrically conductive material and as an electrically self-sensing material with the addition of CNTs, and that the self-sensing properties of UHPFCRC are more sensitive to tensile stress state.
